# M2-4: Financial snapshot and tax-bucket tags

- Milestone: M2
- Branch / worktree: `t/M2-4`, `../YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/M2-4`
- Depends on: M2-3
- Touches (exclusive while running): mcp/ (own files `tools_snapshot*.go`), store/ (read queries in new files, no migration),
  cmd/ (new subcommand file)
- Plan refs: §2 accounts `tax_bucket`, R9a, G6, STATE Decisions 2026-10-29 (category list is PROPOSED)
- YNAB access: none
- Deploy: no

## Goal
`get_financial_snapshot` (R9a) over the current plan, plus `get_goals` and `get_income_events`, and a local way to tag
accounts by tax bucket.

## Scope
- `accounts.tax_bucket` already exists (`0001_mirror.sql`), with `Tx.SetAccountTaxBucket` and `TestTaxBucketSurvivesSync`. Reuse them; no migration.
- `finbot tag-account <account name> <bucket>` and listing of current tags, with buckets taxable, traditional, roth, hsa,
  cash, none. Names, not ids.
- `get_financial_snapshot`: balances by account and tax bucket (untagged shown as `untagged`, never guessed), debt terms
  from the mirror's debt fields, average monthly income and spend, savings rate, goal progress from category targets.
- `get_goals`: category targets and progress from the mirror.
- `get_income_events`: positive transactions categorized to Inflow: Ready to Assign, by date, payee and account. There is no `profile` table or paycheck matcher until M4, so label these as inflows, not confirmed paychecks.
- CSP grouping: the final category list isn't decided. Group by YNAB category group, and expose any CSP labelling only as
  an explicit PROPOSED field. Rename nothing, create nothing in YNAB.
- Report the averaging window and how much history it covers, because categorizing lapsed around 2025. Report uncategorized
  spend as its own figure so a stale plan can't look precise.

- Add tools with `register(auth.ScopeMCP, &sdkmcp.Tool{...}, handler)` from an `init` in a new file; the handler returns only its data and the `Response[T]` wrapper adds freshness. There's no way yet to send a client a specific error such as a bad filter, so use the one M2-3 added next to `errTool`.

## Out of scope
- Anything writing to YNAB, profile data for retirement assumptions (no `profile` table yet), simulators.

## Acceptance (each must be demonstrably checked)
- [ ] Test: `finbot tag-account` sets and lists tags, and rejects an unknown bucket or an ambiguous name.
- [ ] Fixture tests: `get_goals` progress; `get_income_events` includes inflows and excludes transfers, refunds and deleted rows.
- [ ] Fixture tests: bucket totals, debt terms, averages with an uneven window, uncategorized share, goal progress.
- [ ] Test: an untagged account appears as `untagged`.
- [ ] Test: all three tools include data freshness.
- [ ] `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` green

## Result
- Status: DONE
- What changed:
  - `store/snapshot_read.go`: read-only `Accounts` (with tax tag and parsed loan terms), `MonthlyFlows` (income /
    categorized / uncategorized per month), `HistoryRange`, `Goals`, `IncomeLines`. No migration.
  - `cmd/tag_account.go`: `finbot tag-account <account name> <bucket>` (taxable, traditional, roth, hsa, cash, none;
    name matched case-insensitively among live accounts, closed included) and `finbot tag-account [--list]`. Needs only
    `FINBOT_DB_PATH` and `YNAB_BUDGET_ID`, refuses a missing DB file, prints names, never ids. Wired into `cmd/app.go` usage.
  - `mcp/tools_snapshot.go`: `get_financial_snapshot` (open accounts, tax-bucket totals with `untagged`, net worth, loan
    terms in effect today plus history, cash flow over `months` (default 12, max 60) complete months clipped to the first
    transaction, averages per average-length month, uncategorized spend and share, savings rate, spending by YNAB category
    group, `csp_grouping_proposed` note, goal summary), `get_goals`, `get_income_events` (default the last year, limit
    200/max 1000, count and total cover all; labelled "not confirmed paychecks").
  - Income excludes transfers in from off-budget accounts that YNAB categorizes to Ready to Assign (moved savings, not
    income), in both `MonthlyFlows` and `IncomeLines`.
- Acceptance:
  - tag-account sets/lists, rejects unknown bucket and ambiguous name → pass, `go test ./cmd -run TestTagAccount`
  - get_goals progress; get_income_events includes inflows (incl. a split part), excludes transfers, refunds, deleted →
    pass, `go test ./mcp -run 'TestGoals|TestIncomeEvents'`
  - bucket totals, debt terms, averages over an uneven (77-day, 2.5-month) window, uncategorized share, goal progress →
    pass, `go test ./mcp -run 'TestFinancialSnapshot|TestGoals|TestAvgMonthly'`
  - untagged account appears as `untagged` → pass, `TestFinancialSnapshot_BalancesBucketsAndDebts`
  - all three tools carry data freshness → pass, `go test ./mcp -run TestSnapshotTools_CarryFreshness`
  - `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` → pass
- Deviations from brief:
  - The averaging window is day-precise when history starts mid-window (average = total × 30.4375 / days), so a partial
    first month doesn't deflate the averages; `months_covered`, `history_starts`, `months_with_categorized_spending` and
    `months_with_activity` report the coverage.
  - CSP: no group is labelled; only a `csp_grouping_proposed` text field says the grouping is by YNAB group and the CSP
    list is undecided.
  - Closed accounts are left out of the snapshot balances (still listed and taggable in `tag-account`).
  - `none` is a real tag; there is no command to clear a tag back to untagged.
- Follow-ups for backlog:
  - A way to clear a tag (`tag-account <name> --clear`) if wanted.
  - Label CSP buckets once the category list is decided (M4).
  - Paycheck matcher / profile for income events (M4).
  - Liabilities: credit cards and lines of credit have no loan terms in YNAB, so they appear only under accounts.
- Docs follow-ups:
  - CLAUDE.md Build & Run: add `./finbot tag-account [<account name> <bucket>]` (needs `FINBOT_DB_PATH`, `YNAB_BUDGET_ID`).
  - CLAUDE.md Architecture `mcp/`/`store/`: list the three new tools and `store/snapshot_read.go`; note the window and
    income rules above.
